item.title: Ethics Is Always Late, and Society Keeps Rebuilding It: Trust · On Ethics, Addendum
item.description: Trust series · upstream addendum (the system's final chapter): the main essay finished laying out the machine that 'manufactures keeping one's word'; this piece takes apart the question marks left after the lamp turns — when does ethics count as having grown? What separates 'profitable' from 'ought'? Why do humans quarrel over good? Why does every era rebuild it? And how does an ordinary person mount small resistances and act. Ethics is always late, and society keeps rebuilding it.

item.title: Ethics Is Not Moral Preaching; It Is Trust's Water Supply: Trust · On Ethics
item.description: Trust series · upstream (the supply side). The origin essay covered the demand side — how the individual machine survives on predictability. This one covers the supply side — how society manufactures 'keeping one's word,' year after year. Ethics is not moral preaching; it is the pumping station that supplies behavioral predictability. Boundaries are ground out, law is ethics' IOU; ethics has factories, factories have owners, and the owners fight over the factory defaults of right and wrong.

item.title: Trust Is Not Morality; It Is the Chassis of Survival: The Origin of Trust
item.description: Trust series · Origin (the foundational outline). Trust is not a moral virtue; it is gregarious creatures' dependence on the predictability of others' behavior — a survival apparatus. When the apparatus breaks, people panic first; at the extreme, they run to the two ends; and the way they run gets welded in by a security model for life. The individual side covers 'how to walk,' the group side covers 'where the era is heading' — this piece is the ground they both stand on: what trust is, why we must trust, and why the crack never closes.

item.title: Individuals Are Changing Currency; the Group Awaits Recasting: Trust Crisis · Group-Side Observation
item.description: The individual side covered 'how you should walk.' One question remains: what state is the whole era in? Seven symptoms, one index, five boundaries — the old trust system is failing as a whole, and society has entered the credit-recasting period.

item.title: Why Does Modern Rest Leave You More Exhausted? “Energy Hemorrhage” Is the Biggest Scam
item.description: Three hours of short videos, lying in bed until 2 p.m. on the weekend, a tenth rewatch of Friends — and on Monday morning you still feel run over by a truck. Where's the problem? Not too little rest; you simply never learned how to rest.
